aAbout: Flightradar24 shows real-time aircraft positions built from ADS-B, MLAT, radar and FAA data fed by roughly 45,000 volunteer receivers, with airport departure and arrival boards, aircraft photos and deep flight history. Its consumer plans layer on features — up to 365 days of history, full aircraft details (age, serial, squawk, vertical speed), 15+ weather layers, aeronautical charts and oceanic tracks — and its iOS/Android apps, including 3D and cockpit views, are widely considered the best in flight tracking.
aStrengths: Flightradar24 is the deeper tool for watching the sky itself: a receiver network of roughly 45,000 feeders, up to 365 days of flight history, full aircraft details, 15+ live weather layers, ATC boundaries, aeronautical charts, oceanic tracks, CSV export and airport boards with live ETAs. Its apps are best-in-class for planespotting, and it reports more than 1,000,000 subscribers across its plans.
bAbout: FlightAware tracks flights with a focus on status and operations: live flight status, schedules, airport delay information and flight history, backed by premium accounts that add flight alerts, 3, 5 or 8 months of historical data and saved airports and aircraft. Around the consumer tracker sits a serious aviation-data business — Aviator for general-aviation owners, Global for business-jet operators, FBO Toolbox for airports, and the Firehose data feed for commercial customers.
bStrengths: FlightAware is the deeper tool for what a flight is doing: detailed status and schedules, airport delay and operations information, and a data business that airlines, operators and aviation professionals rely on. Its premium history (3, 5 or 8 months), GA-focused Aviator suite and business-jet Global product serve working aviation in ways an enthusiast map does not try to.
betterAnswer: For most casual and enthusiast users, Flightradar24 is the better default: the richer map, longer history and better apps. For travellers checking a flight's real status, anyone around US airports, and aviation professionals, FlightAware's status, delay and data depth wins. They overlap enough that price and the free tiers settle it for many people — try both free before paying either.

faqs.a: Both aggregate ADS-B, MLAT, radar and official data (including FAA data), so live positions are broadly comparable. FlightAware is often stronger on flight status, schedules and US delay information; Flightradar24's roughly 45,000-receiver network gives it very dense live position coverage. Accuracy varies by region and flight — neither is perfect for every tail number.

intro: Flightradar24 and FlightAware are the two biggest names in flight tracking, and they split the job differently. Flightradar24 (Sweden, founded 2006) is the enthusiast's global map: real-time aircraft positions from a vast volunteer receiver network, rich aircraft detail and polished apps. FlightAware is the American aviation-data company: flight status, schedules and airport operations are its home turf, with premium accounts for individuals and data products like Firehose for the industry. Both track the same sky — what differs is depth, audience and price.
pricingA: Free Basic tier with limited features. Paid consumer plans — Silver, Gold and Business — unlock 60+ premium features, with a 7-day free trial and pricing that varies by region (2026 reviews list Silver at roughly $12.99/year on annual billing). The Flightradar24 API is sold separately from the subscriptions.
pricingB: Free consumer tracking tier with limits and advertising. Premium accounts for individuals add alerts, longer history and saved airports/aircraft; the professional products (Aviator, Global, FBO Toolbox) and data feeds such as Firehose are priced separately for operators and businesses.

verdictA: Choose Flightradar24 if you track for the love of it — planespotting, following aircraft globally, digging into history and aircraft detail, or wanting the best mobile apps and 3D views.
verdictB: Choose FlightAware if you track for a reason — a specific flight's status, US airport delays, a general-aviation aircraft you operate, or aviation data for a business.
worldEye: If you mainly want to glance at the sky rather than study it, WorldEye shows live flights free on a 3D globe — no signup — alongside live ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras in the same view.
